paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples with a larger number of examples
model_annotation: The diagram illustrates the performance comparison between the proposed ST-ES method and a random example selection baseline, as measured by the minimum Average Displacement Error (minADE₂₀) across varying numbers of in-context examples. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” spans from 0 to 15 and is linearly scaled with integer tick marks at intervals of 1, representing the count of examples used. The y-axis, labeled “minADE₂₀ (←)”, ranges from 15.00 to 17.00 and is linearly scaled with tick marks at intervals of 0.50, indicating the error metric in arbitrary units. The ST-ES line is depicted as a solid blue line with circular markers, starting at a value of 17.00 at 0 examples and decreasing monotonically to 14.98 at 15 examples, with intermediate values including 15.10 at 1 example and 14.99 at 15 examples. The Random line is shown as a solid orange line with circular markers, beginning at 16.75 at 0 examples and remaining nearly constant at approximately 16.50 from 1 to 15 examples, with values of 16.50 at 1 example and 16.50 at 15 examples.

model_annotations.English: This line plot compares the performance of two methods, ST-ES and Random, as measured by minADE₂₀ (in units of meters, indicated by the arrow), across varying numbers of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 15. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” uses a linear scale with tick marks at regular intervals of 1, spanning from 0 to 15. The y-axis, labeled “minADE₂₀ (←)”, uses a linear scale with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.5, ranging from 15.00 to 17.00. The ST-ES method is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, starting at a value of approximately 17.00 at 0 examples and decreasing steadily to approximately 14.90 at 15 examples. The Random method is represented by an orange line with circular markers, starting at approximately 16.75 at 0 examples and remaining nearly constant at approximately 16.50 for the entire range up to 15 examples.
